messages:
elaine_support: Hey team — Acme reported SSE streams that close mid-response after ~30s of silence. They see a 200 and a few events, then connection drops. They sit behind Cloudflare Workers -> ALB -> our origin. Anyone seen similar?

mike_infra: That pattern screams proxy idle timeout or buffering. Can you paste the curl + headers and any origin logs you have?

elaine_support: Repro I used:
```
curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat/abc' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
```
Response shows:
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream
event: message
data: {"id":"msg_1","text":"hello"}

# ~30s pause from server (no data)
*** Failed to receive HTTP2 DATA: ECONNRESET
```
Origin nginx error log around same time: `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`

ingrid_sre: Do we send heartbeats reliably? ALB default idle timeout is 60s but customers sometimes set shorter. Cloudflare may also buffer and change the timing. Are they using HTTP/2 between CF and ALB? HTTP/2 flow/windowing can hide heartbeats.

sam_custeng: Customer config: ALB idle timeout set to 30s (they said they lowered it for scale). Cloudflare in front has a Worker that proxies requests — that Worker rewrites headers. They also enable 'Argo Smart Routing' but not sure that matters. Customer says they see disconnects consistently after ~30s.

mike_infra: Confirmed: if ALB idle timeout == 30s and origin doesn't send any bytes for 30s, ALB will close the connection. SSE can be silent for a while. Two mitigations: (1) send SSE comment/heartbeat every ~10s from app (i.e. `: keepalive\n\n`) and flush, (2) set ALB idle timeout > expected silent window (e.g., 120s). Also ensure nginx `proxy_buffering off;` and `proxy_read_timeout` > idle window.

elaine_support: I ran tcpdump between CF and ALB during repro:
```
14:01:12.123 IP client > cf-in: GET /v1/streams/chat/abc
14:01:12.456 IP cf > alb: GET /v1/streams/chat/abc
14:01:12.800 IP origin > alb: SSE data chunk
14:01:43.900 IP alb > origin: FIN, ack (idle timeout triggered)
```
so ALB is doing the close.

ingrid_sre: Cloudflare Workers can buffer and coalesce chunks — if CF doesn't see bytes it might hold and then send them as a big chunk which confuses ALB idle timers. Ask customer to bypass CF (direct to ALB) as a quick isolate. If bypass avoids the drop then the worker path is likely rebuffering.

sam_custeng: Suggested customer test steps I sent:
- Direct curl to ALB origin (skip CF) with `-N` and observe for >60s
- If direct connection stays open, try toggling Worker to `fetch(request, { cf: { cacheEverything: false } })` or ensure the Worker streams response (don't read whole body and re-emit)

mike_infra: Quick workaround we recommend in KB: add a lightweight SSE comment heartbeat every 10s and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked + flush after each event. Example server snippet (node):
```js
res.write(': hb\\n\\n'); // send comment to keep proxies alive
res.flushHeaders(); // if using express + compression disabled
```
Also nginx conf: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection '';` and `proxy_read_timeout 300s;`

elaine_support: Customer tried heartbeat at 15s and still saw drop behind CF+ALB. When they bypassed CF it was stable. So we think Worker path buffers then ALB sees silence and closes.

ingrid_sre: Action items:
- ask customer to set ALB idle timeout >= 120s for now (if feasible)
- disable any Worker-level buffering or re-stream, or temporarily bypass CF to confirm
- add server-side heartbeat every 10s (best-effort) and disable gzip/compression on that route
- we should update support KB with explicit Cloudflare Worker notes and example Worker streaming code that forwards body chunks instead of aggregating.

sam_custeng: I've opened an escalation ticket with them and requested a short window to test ALB timeout change + bypass. Also gave them a sample Worker snippet to stream: `const res = await fetch(originReq); return new Response(res.body, { headers: res.headers });` (don't call `await res.text()`).

incident-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026 | P2 | "SSE client disconnects behind Cloudflare Worker + ALB"

mike_infra: TL;DR: not a Redwood runtime bug — interaction of Cloudflare Worker buffering + ALB idle timeout. Recommended immediate workaround = heartbeat + bump idle timeout + bypass CF for validation. Follow up: update docs + add a small test harness for customers to validate streaming through common proxies. :thumbsup:
